office_does: The U.S. Representative votes on federal law and the federal budget for a two-year term, oversees the executive branch, and helps constituents with federal agencies.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Marilyn Strickland, a former Tacoma mayor in Congress since 2021, took 47.3% in the primary. Republican Chris D. Chung, a Lakewood pharmacist who took 31.4%, has stated concerns but few specific positions.

candidates.summary: Congresswoman since 2021, former Tacoma mayor and House Armed Services member, running on her local-project record, health-care and food-aid protections, and opposition to tariffs.
highlights: Mayor of Tacoma 2010-2017; Chief Deputy Whip and New Democrat Coalition Whip [S1][S2][S4]
Voted for the final FY2026 NDAA and against cutting military aid to Israel [S17][S18]
Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes Trump's tariffs and health-care and food-aid cuts [S1][S12]
Voted against the federal girls' sports and born-alive bills; endorsed by Planned Parenthood [S1][S13][S14]
Voted for the HALT Fentanyl Act [S16]

taxes.basis: Voted against H.R. 1 and opposes tariffs; no stated plank on progressive revenue.

spending.basis: Backs preserving and expanding SNAP, WIC, LIHEAP and housing aid and touts $50 million in projects; voted for the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act.

safety.basis: Voted for the HALT Fentanyl Act and cites funding for police and firefighters; no stated enforcement or prevention agenda beyond that.

climate.basis: Works to 'boost renewable energy,' voted to keep California's vehicle-emission waiver, and is endorsed by LCV and Sierra Club.

experience.basis: In Congress since 2021 after two terms as Tacoma mayor; holds House whip and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Chief Deputy Whip, New Democrat Coalition Whip and chair of ASPIRE PAC, working through party and caucus structures.

immigration.basis: Voted against the Laken Riley Act; no further immigration statements in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Pledges to protect Medicare and make care more affordable and backs reinstating ACA subsidies, all within the current system.

social.basis: Reproductive Freedom Caucus liaison, reintroduced the Abortion is Health Care Everywhere Act, and voted against H.R. 28 and H.R. 21.

defense.basis: Voted for the FY2026 NDAA and against cutting Israel military aid and says Israel has the right to defend itself; also questioned the Iran operations and backed the Iran War Powers resolution.

candidates.summary: Lakewood pharmacist and pharmacy owner for 33 years, who ran in the 2024 and 2025 primaries; his statement names concerns rather than specific policies.
highlights: Pharmacist and owner of a Tacoma (Lakewood) pharmacy for 33 years [S1]
Focus on easing family burdens, access to education and health care, and respect for veterans [S1]
Ran for Insurance Commissioner in 2024 as 'Prefers Democratic Party'; now 'Prefers Republican Party' [S3][S6]

experience.basis: No elected office; small-business pharmacist whose 2024 and 2025 primary bids drew under 7% each in reported returns.
